Borrowed from Middle Low German ambacht or its source Old Saxon ambaht, from Proto-Germanic *ambahtaz (compare Old High German ambahti, ambaht (“service”), Old Saxon ambaht (“service”)), from Gaulish ambaxtos, from Proto-Celtic *ambaxtos.

parole.significato: decree; executive order (regulation that is subordinate to legislative statutes, specifies them or lays down how they a…
parole.testo: asettaa (“to place, set”) + -us. Originally “placing, setting”; the legal sense “decree” from the Middle Ages, probably as a semantic loan from another language (compare German Gesetz from setzen), perhaps a semantic loan from Middle Low German gesette.
Ultimately from Middle Low German echt possibly through Swedish. Cognate with Swedish äkta and German echt.
Borrowed from Middle Low German hane (compare German Hahn (“tap, faucet”)).
Possibly borrowed from Middle Low German [Term?].
From Middle Low German holt.

Probably borrowed from Middle Low German hȫge (“feast, banquet”); the vocalism may be explained by delabialization in the easternmost dialects of Middle Low German. Cognate with Ingrian häät, Karelian heät and possibly Võro hähk.
Borrowed from Middle Low German hövel.
From Middle Low German jacht. Compare Estonian jaht, Low German Jacht, Dutch jacht, German Jagd.
kaakin + puu, from dialectal kaaki, kaakki, from Middle Low German kāk
Borrowed from Middle Low German gaffel.
Borrowed from Middle Low German gicht (compare Swedish gikt).

Borrowed from Middle Low German kīl (“wedge”), possibly but not necessarily through Swedish kil (“wedge”). Even an older Proto-Germanic borrowing has been suggested, but this runs into phonetic difficulties (the Low German word derives from earlier *kīþla-).

parole.significato: a type of richly decorated drinking vessel, made of wood, with handles on both sides
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German kouwse.
Borrowed from Middle Low German grēve, ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *garāfijō.

parole.significato: any of the traditional types of foods baked inside a loaf of bread, particularly common in Eastern Finland
parole.testo: Multiple theories: * a borrowing from Middle Low German kûke (“cake”) * related to kukku and kukkula (“hill”), e.g. "round thing" * shortened form of kukkaro (“purse”) * related to kukko (etymology 1): this theory is not semantically convincing

parole.significato: cock, dick, prick, schlong (singular) penis, (plural) male genitalia
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Middle Low German kul, kulle (“testicle”) (compare Dutch kul).

parole.significato: mortar, plaster (mixture of lime, cement or gypsum, as well as sand and water)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German plāster (“plaster, gypsum, mortar, cement”), itself ultimately from Latin emplastrum. Doublet of laastari.
Borrowed from Middle Low German last.
From Middle Low German lecher.
Borrowed from Middle Low German līste with the suffix + -e.

parole.significato: compartment, box (small compartment or subdivided space, e.g. in furniture such as a drawer)
parole.testo: Unknown; possibly from Middle Low German lok (“hole; recess”) (compare German Loch) with + -ero (compare dialectal lokko).
mit- + -ata, probably borrowed from Middle Low German mēten, metten (third-person singular present form mit). An older Germanic borrowing has also been proposed, but runs into phonetic difficulties.

parole.significato: catfish, sheatfish (freshwater catfish of the genus Silurus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German monne.
Probably borrowed from Middle Low German nap, if not an older Germanic borrowing.
nimi (“name”) + -ttäin (distributive plural), ultimately a calque of Middle Low German nēmelīk (compare German nämlich)
Borrowed from Middle Low German pant.

parole.significato: lance (weapon of war, consisting of a long shaft or handle and a steel blade or head; a spear carried by horsemen)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German spētze, from Old Saxon spiot, from Proto-West Germanic *speut (“spear”).

parole.significato: game (activity described by a set of rules, especially for the purpose of entertainment)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German spel, from Proto-West Germanic *spil. Doublet of pila.
Borrowed from Middle Low German vracht. Cognate with English freight.
Borrowed from Middle Low German recht, or alternatively (less likely, in light of vocalism) from Swedish riktig (“right, correct, genuine”).

parole.significato: ring-shaped baked good, such as a bagel, pretzel or donut
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German kringel.
From Middle Low German Ritter, possibly via Old Swedish riddare. First attested in the 15th century.
Borrowed from Middle Low German vrouwe.
Borrowed from Middle Low German krūt, short for büssenkrūt, bussenkrût (“gunpowder”) (originally krūt meant "spice, herb").
Borrowed from Middle Low German schrūve.
rypä- (“cluster, bunch”) + -le, or alternatively a borrowing from Middle Low German drûfele.

parole.significato: fyke net, fyke (type of fish-trap consisting of tubular nets that are supported by hoops)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Middle Low German rǖse. Cognate with Estonian rüsa, Ingrian rysä, Karelian ryšä /ryžä, Votic rüsä, Swedish ryssja (“fish-trap”) and German Reuse (“fish-trap”).
Borrowed from Middle Low German schrādære, compare Karelian riätäri.

parole.significato: rig (rigging of a sailing ship or other such craft)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German takel.
From Middle Low German dīrk, dīderik. Adapted with + -(i)kka. Cognate with Swedish dyrk.
From Middle Low German touwe.
From Middle Low German trān.
Swedish traktera + -ata, from Middle Low German trakteren, from Latin tractō.
Borrowed from Middle Low German stōp.

parole.significato: guard, sentry, sentinel (person who or thing that protects something)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle Low German wacht.

parole.significato: an unspecified piece of apparatus, or one for which one does not know a real name; gimmick, thingamajig, gadget, contra…
parole.testo: Unknown. Related to Karelian veh­keh, reflecting earlier *vehgeh. If related to Estonian vehkima (“to swing (back and forth)”), possibly from Middle Low German vechten.
Borrowed either from North Germanic (compare Old Norse enda) or from Middle Low German ende, in either case ultimately from Proto-Germanic *anþi. Compare Estonian ent (“but”).
Borrowed either from Swedish handske (“glove”) or directly from Middle Low German hantsche.

parole.significato: Wednesday (day of the week; the third day of the week in Finland and in the ISO 8601 standard)
parole.testo: keski- (“mid-, middle”) + viikko (“week”), a calque either of Middle Low German middewēke (compare modern German Mittwoch), or of a seemingly unattested Old Swedish word (compare Old Norse miðvikudagr (literally “mid-week day”)). parole.significato: Monday (day of the week; the first day of the week in Finland and in the ISO 8601 standard)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old Swedish mānadagher, or from Middle Low German māndach; ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *mānini dag.

Possibly borrowed from Middle Low German ovel, ovele, from Proto-Germanic *ubilaz. Alternatively related to dialectal evelä, Estonian õel (“wicked, cruel, savage, evil, mean”) and Votic õjõla (Pummala).

parole.significato: jury, panel (body of judges in a competition)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old Swedish rāþ (compare modern Swedish råd (“council”), German Rat (“council”)) or from Middle Low German rāt. Doublet of roti.
Probably borrowed from Middle Low German brôk with + -e; alternatively, an older borrowing from Proto-Germanic *brōks (implying Proto-Finnic *rook'ëh).

Most likely borrowed from Swedish valt, the supine of välja (“to choose, elect”), as in many card games the trump suit is nominated. parole.significato: rent (payment made by a tenant or user of a service)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vookra (compare Karelian vuokra, Ludian vuogr; no more cognates are known), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wōkraz (“interest; usury, gain; increase”), or alternatively a more recent borrowing from Middle Low German wôker.
